MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  AUGUST 28, 2023
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5:30 P.M.

  The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and teleconferenced from various
  locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

  MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Silverstein called the meeting to order at 5:30 p.m.

  ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Bruce Silverstein; Mayor Pro Tem Steve Uhring; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Doug Stewart

  PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 5:30 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

  Conference with L_egal Counsel — Existing litigation pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9(d)(1):

  1.  Case Name: City’s Petition to Form Malibu USD from Territory in the Santa
  Monica-Malibu USD

  Conference with Legal Counsel —— Anticipated Litigation

  Number of potential cases: (1)

  REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Silverstein called the meeting to order at 7:07 pm.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 28, 2023
  Page 2 of 11

i  ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Bruce Silverstein; Mayor Pro Tern Steve Uhring; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Doug Stewart

  ALSO PRESENT: Monica Castello, Deputy City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey
  Pettij ohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy,
  Environmental Sustainability Director; Richard Mollica, Planning Director; Susan Duefias,
  Public Safety Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Jason Lawrence, Deputy City
  Clerk; and Kate Manisco, Recreation Manager

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Dennis Smith led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Deputy City Attorney Castillo reported that the meeting convened at 5 :30 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9(d)(1) and 54956.9(d)(4), with all Councilmembers present. She stated the Council
  discussed the item listed on the closed session agenda and took no reportable action.

  REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  August 17, 2023, with the amended agenda posted on August 25, 2023.

  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

  MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring moved, and Councilmember Riggins seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

  ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  John Mazza announced a weekly six-week docent training course at the Adamson
  House beginning on September 20, 2023.

  Tracey Lovric, Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority (MRCA),
  commented on two recent incidents where a person physically and verbally
  interfered with MRCA contractors’ installation of directional signposts in an
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 28, 2023
  Page 3 of11

  easement in Escondido Canyon managed by MRCA and owned by the Santa
  Monica Mountains Conservancy.

  Jo Drummond discussed code enforcement, the communications tower at Santa
  Monica College (SMC), and the large tent for a wedding on Broad Beach. She
  discussed formula retail ordinance enforcement to ensure local businesses were not
  displaced by chain stores.

  Robert Brinkman discussed the Parks and Recreation Commission, the Seawolves
  coach staffing change, and the formation of the Malibu Marlins swim club. He
  discussed the staff and Parks and Recreation Commission review of the Malibu
  Marlins application for swimming pool usage.

  Bill Sampson discussed the recent wedding on Broad Beach Road and provided a
  presentation of the tent application.

  Kraig Hill discussed vehicles speeding on Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) on
  Wednesday and Saturday nights. He commented on the Navy offshore testing that
  produced sonic booms and stated his concern about effects on marine life.
ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Fireball Lawrence, Malibu Arts Commission, thanked Anne Buxie for serving as
  Poet Laureate and announced Changing 0f the Verse poetry event would be held
  September 28, 2023, at 5:00 p.m. at City Hall. He thanked the artists who
  participated in the summer art exhibition and announced the opening of the Wes
  Van Dyke exhibit was scheduled for September 16, 2023 at City Hall. He
  announced the new art piece by Maureen Haldeman would be exhibited for one
  year in the multi-purpose room at City Hall as part of a rotating art program.

  City Manager McClary announced the Malibu High School (MHS) local coastal
  program amendment (LCPA) would be reviewed by the California Coastal
  Commission (CCC) on September 9, 2023, and the revised LCPA would be
  reviewed by the Council before certification by the CCC. He stated that the MHS
  coastal development permit would be considered by the Flaming Commission on
  September 5, 2023. He discussed tropical storm Hilary and stated that the City
  experienced minor damage from the significant amount of rain and that the City
  declared a local emergency and would be applying for disaster funds. He announced
  that City Clerk Pettijohn had achieved her Certified Municipal Clerk designation
  from the International Institute of Municipal Clerks.

  City Clerk Pettij ohn thanked City Manager McClary for the recognition and stated
  she loved serving the community.

  City Manager McClary announced that all parks would be open for the Labor Day
  holiday, but the swimming pool and Senior Center would be closed. He announced
  that the next Library Speaker Series featuring a discussion by Scott Freeman on the
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 28, 2023
  Page 4 ofll

  Beatles album Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band would be held September
  20, 2023 at City Hall. He stated that staff met with Los Angeles County and SMC
  officials to discuss the communications tower and an agreement was made for the
  tower to be repainted a neutral color and a possible application by SMC for a height
  variance. He stated that a conditional use permit (CUP) needed to be issued before
  the tower could operate. He stated that the farmers’ market was discussed and the
  college and the County would help the Cornucopia Foundation return the market to
  its previous location at the college to avoid disruption to the schedule. He stated
  that the temporary use permit for the farmers’ market at Legacy Park would expire
  on October 7, 2023. He stated topics for the upcoming Council meeting on
  September ll, 2023 included fire season safety preparations, accessory dwelling
  units (ADU), outdoor warning sirens, and Woolsey Fire fee waivers. In response to
  Mayor Silverstein, he stated County staff would confirm with the Sheriff
  Department if the tower issue would delay opening the Sheriff substation.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Uhring, Deputy City Manager Brown stated that
  SMC had not received a certificate of completion from the State.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, stated Sheriff
  staff would be present at the Chili Cook-off over the Labor Day weekend, which
  also marked the last weekend of the beach team’s presence in Malibu. He reported
  that 17 cars were towed to the temporary tow yard. He discussed a recent fatal
  stabbing at Las Tunas Beach during a domestic violence incident. He reported the
  special assignment deputies attended training on vehicle theft and recreational
  vehicle (RV) homelessness encampment protocol. He stated that the RV that was
  parked for two years at Las Tunas Beach had been towed. He reported a burglary
  occurred that day on Malibu Road and the suspects were taken into custody. He
  discussed enforcement at Nobu over the past two weekends and stated 27 traffic
  citations were issued and parking enforcement was forthcoming.

  Mayor Uhring stated that he observed speeding vehicles on Malibu Canyon Road.

ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Riggins discussed special event permits (SEP) and the Broad
  Beach wedding and recommended the Zoning Ordinance Revisions and Code
  Enforcement Subcommittee (ZORACES) review regulations.

  In response to Councilmember Stewart, Flaming Director Mollica stated the
  Council would consider a temporary use permit (TUP) ordinance in October, but
  SEPs would not be addressed as they were in a different chapter of the code.

  Councilmember Riggins stated that SEP rules should be tightened because the
  wedding event was not representative of the application. She commented on
  damage to the dunes and stated that the size and engineering required to facilitate
  the tent structure was beyond the scope of the SEP.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 28, 2023
  Page 5 of 11

  Mayor Silverstein indicated support for ZORACES review of the general SEP, but
  stated the Broad Beach Road wedding violated the current regulation.

  Councilmember Riggins stated that everyone should be on the same page regarding
  what was allowed on residents’ properties and the intent of permitting types. In
  response to Mayor Silverstein, she stated that residents needed direction provided
  on expectations of what was allowed on their properties. She congratulated City
  Clerk Pettij ohn and thanked her for her service. She stated residents would receive
  brush clearance compliance letters from the Fire Department.

  In response to Councilmember Riggins, Community Services Director Riesgo
  discussed vendor selection for recreational programs and stated that a discussion
  item on the process would be presented to the Parks and Recreation Commission.

  Councilmember Riggins stated she attended the August Malibu Library Speaker
  Series event which featured NASA Aerospace Engineer Dr. Aprille Ericsson and
  encouraged the public’s participation in future events.

  Councilmember Stewart stated that he attended the August Malibu Library Speaker
  Series event. He thanked the Volunteers on Patrol, Community Emergency
  Response Team, and first responders for their work during Tropical Storm Hilary.
  He discussed the Broad Beach wedding, staff time spent, and intent of the SEP
  ordinance. He suggested considering a Loud and Unruly Gathering Ordinance
  (LUGO) and the potential enforcement tools under that type of ordinance which
  were in proportion to the disruption the event caused. He thanked Poison Free
  Malibu for organizing weed clearance at the headlands and the Malibu Lagoon. He
  discussed the Work Plan Workshop and potential usage of the City’s vacant land.
  He discussed ADUs and suggested concerns addressed in public correspondence
  be incorporated into the future agenda item. He discussed a proposal for a funding
  program to support school sponsored athletics for elementary and middle schools.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item to consider
  supporting alternative youth athletic programs.

  Councilmember Stewart congratulated City Clerk Pettij ohn on her achievements.

  Councilmember Grisanti congratulated City Clerk Pettij ohn and thanked her for her
  service. He stated that he attended the Work Plan Workshop and found it
  productive. He stated that he received calls about the Broad Beach wedding,
  Tropical Storm Hilary, and the earthquake. He discussed racing in and around the
  City and suggested warning signage as a deterrent.

  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring recommended the public Visit the Adamson House. He
  requested brush clearance by the MRCA on the trail around Bluffs Park. He
  indicated support for consideration of a contribution from the City to the youth
  sports programs proposal and recommended proponents provide goals for the
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 28, 2023
  Page 6 of 11

  program’s independence from the City, enrollment figures, and examples of
  community funding not associated with schools. He discussed the management of
  the City-owned Malibu Lumber Yard, reports of tenant lease termination, and the
  importance of supporting local businesses. He discussed code enforcement and a
  recent party in Big Rock at the same house Where previous unpermitted parties
  occurred. He discussed the Broad Beach wedding event, provided a timeline of
  activity, SEP conditions, settlement agreement terms, and the message the
  settlement agreement sent to the public and staff.

  Mayor Silverstein recommended individuals who submit written comments also
  speak at the meeting or over Zoom. He congratulated City Clerk Pettijohn and
  thanked her for her efforts. He discussed the City’s response to tropical storm
  Hilary and the recent earthquake. He stated that he attended the Special Work Plan
  Workshop and that it was a great team-building experience. He discussed
  complaints of public speakers being cut off after three minutes and the importance
  of rules being applied impartially. He discussed recent improved coverage by the
  Malibu Times of City events. He discussed the Broad Beach Road wedding event
  and misrepresentations made at Council meetings.

  ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

:1  Item Nos. 3.B.5., 3.B.7., and 3.B.8. were pulled by the Council.

  MOTION  Mayor Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Uhring seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item Nos. 3.B.5., 3.B.7., and 3.B.8. The
  question was called, and the motion carried unanimously, Councilmembers Riggins
  and Stewart abstaining from Item No. 3.B.3.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  69935—70136 on the register from the General Fund and direct the City

  names, for the purposes stated on the respective demands in a total amount
  of $2,622,336.86. City of Malibu payroll check number 5366-5367 and

  City Council Regular meeting, August 22, 2022 Malibu City Council

  Resolution Extending the Declaration of the COVID-l9 Local Emergency

  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 23-42 ratifying the

  The following items were pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  Professional Services Agreement with California Skateparks
  Recommended Action: Authorize the Mayor to execute a sole source
  Professional Services Agreement with California Skateparks related to

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  motion to authorize the Mayor to execute a sole source Professional
  Services Agreement with California Skateparks related to repairs of the
  Temporary Skate Park. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

  8.  Amend the Salary Ranges for FY 2023-24
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 23-38 amending the Salary
  Ranges for FY 2023-24.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring moved, and Councilmember Riggins seconded a
  motion to adopt Resolution No. 23-38 amending the Salary Ranges for FY
  2023-24. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

  Mayor Silverstein confirmed with staff that there were no public speakers
  for items pulled from the Consent Calendar.

ITEM 4  ORDINANCES AND PUBLIC HEARINGS

  Update Regarding Zoning Map Amendment No. 17-002 and Zoning Text
  Amendment No. 20-001 (Sea View Hotel Project)
  Recommended Action: 1) After the City Attomey reads the title of the ordinance,
  introduce on first reading Ordinance No. 509, an ordinance of the City of Malibu
  amending Zoning Map Amendment (ZMA) No. 17-002 and Zoning Text
  Amendment (ZTA) No. 20-001 to effectuate previous amendments made to Local
  Coastal Program Amendment (LCPA) No. 16-006 for the Sea View Hotel Project
  as adopted by Ordinance No. 491 on September 13, 2021 and amended by
  Ordinance No. 508 on July 10, 2023 pursuant to the conditional certification action
  taken by the California Coastal Commission (CCC) on February 8, 2023 to rezone
  and change the land use designation of the properties located at 22741 and 22729
  Pacific Coast Highway from Community Commercial (CC) to Commercial Visitor
  Serving-2 (CV-2), a new Seaview Hotel Overlay District with associated
  development standards, including a proposed floor area ratio of 0.52 for the public
  benefits provided by the proj ect (the amendments to the ZMA and ZTA are
  corollary to LCPA and will not be effective until the LCPA is certified by the CCC),
  and finding the action to require no further environmental review and/or to be
  exempt from such review under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA);
  and 2) Direct staffto schedule a second reading and adoption of Ordinance No. 509
  for the September 11, 2023 Regular City Council meeting.

  Planning Director Mollica presented the staff report.

  The Council directed questions to staff.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of August 28, 2023
  Page 9 of 11

  Speaker: Fred Gaines

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to
  the table for discussion.

MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved, and Councilmember Riggins seconded a motion
  to 1) introduce on first reading Ordinance No. 509, an ordinance of the City of
  Malibu amending Zoning Map Amendment (ZMA) No. 17-002 and Zoning Text
  Amendment (ZTA) No. 20-001 to effectuate previous amendments made to Local
  Coastal Program Amendment (LCPA) No. 16-006 for the Sea View Hotel Proj ect
  as adopted by Ordinance No. 491 on September 13, 2021 and amended by
  Ordinance No. 508 on July 10, 2023 pursuant to the conditional certification action
  taken by the California Coastal Commission (CCC) on February 8, 2023 to rezone
  and change the land use designation of the properties located at 22741 and 22729
  Pacific Coast Highway from Community Commercial (CC) to Commercial Visitor
  Serving-2 (CV-2), a new SeaView Hotel Overlay District with associated
  development standards, including a proposed floor area ratio of 0.52 for the public
  benefits provided by the project (the amendments to the ZMA and ZTA are
  corollary to LCPA and will not be effective until the LCPA is certified by the CCC),
  and finding the action to require no further environmental review and/or to be
  exempt from such review under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA);
  and 2) direct staff to schedule a second reading and adoption of Ordinance No. 509
  for the September 11, 2023 Regular City Council meeting.

  Deputy City Attorney Castillo read the title of the ordinance.

  The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

RECESS  At 8:25 p.m., Mayor Silverstein recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 8:37
